title: In one MICrONS mouse, RF location matching removed the LM and RL movie-spectrum excess over V1 but not the AL excess; in its digital twin, weights, location and pairing each gave a third
abstract: Question: in higher mouse visual areas (HVAs), cvPCA response spectra decay faster than in V1. What makes this happen? We used one MICrONS mouse (13 two-photon scans, 6 natural-movie clips with repeats, V1, LM, RL, AL) and the released digital twin, which has one shared core and a per-neuron readout (location and feature weights). In vivo, the hierarchy slope of alpha was 0.208 (95% interval over scans 0.123 to 0.292; 13 of 13 scans), as in a parallel study. V1 units covered a wider part of the visual field. When V1 samples were matched to the RF locations of each HVA sample, the LM and RL excess over V1 disappeared (-0.008, 0.014), but AL stayed steeper (0.074; 0.071 with reliability also matched). The twin gave 81% of the in vivo slope on the same clips and the same location-matched pattern. An exact readout-exchange decomposition of the twin split the AL excess (0.090) into readout weights 0.029, readout location 0.027 and area-specific weight-location pairing 0.033, each positive in 6 of 6 scans; by the pre-set rule no single part dominates. AL weights gave 80% of the AL increase in top-5 variance share. Exploratory checks show that the exp output nonlinearity and the luminance-locked first core direction do not make the weight part, and that narrower coverage gives about two thirds of the location part. Limitations: one mouse, four areas, a model-based decomposition, 6 twin scans.
